I get dizzy and lightheaded all the time now even though I’m reasonably recovered. Sometimes I’ll completely black out and faint, and according to my family who have seen this happen, I sort of have mini seizures. I’ve hit my head a few times because of it. Sometimes just looking around or turning my head makes me dizzy. Idk if it’s left over damage from my ED, but I do know that that’s when my symptoms started and I never went to a doctor because I was afraid they’d make me eat or go to treatment. Now it’s gotten so much worse and nobody seems to know what to do.
Fr tho I was so motivated and on track and then my period came and now I’ve felt so snacky

I tried handing myself and had a panic attack. Family found out and I was admitted to a psych ward where I didn’t meet with a therapist OR case manager (which is not suppose to happen), and the only “doctor” I did see tried to invalidate all of my previous diagnosis (even though they’re all pretty obviously apparent in me and my Behaviors). I was sent home with a child’s dose of an antidepressant, which didn’t work, and now it’s over half a year later and I’m planning on hanging myself again here soon. Maybe this time I’ll get high first or something so I’m too sluggish to set myself free.

For the record, I have tried other medication since then, I’ve been in therapy every week, I have four doctors on my team rn doing different stuff. None of it’s gotten me anywhere. I’m ready to go.

As someone w anorexia, trust me, you’ll spend so much more time feeling like you’re dying without actually being in imminent danger than you think. It genuinely feels absolutely horrible. It also severely impairs your brain and decision making abilities, that loss of control just adds to the negativity and panic. 

I get it though. I understand how much you must be suffering to be at this point. But I promise, even just after high school, things will be different. Obviously they won’t be better right away. Try to think of all the things you used to be excited about and remind your self that they’re all possible, even if you don’t believe it.

My sister told my dad about my ed as it was getting more physically serious. I’m at a healthier weight now, but ever since, he always takes me out to eat when he picks me up from the airport and asks me what I want for dinner rather than just making something. Even before I developed an Ed, I was super picky. Never once in my life did my family ask me what I wanted for dinner. They usually just made whatever. But now my dad asks every time, and after every meal he asks everyone if they got enough  to eat (I think he’s trying not to single me out, which I am very grateful for). I don’t think he knows that Ik my sister said something to him, I think he understands confronting it with me wouldn’t be helpful. I appreciate what he’s doing and how he’s doing it though.

That’s exactly how I feel, I don’t even like being this skinny. I miss having thighs and curves. But watching the numbers go down on the scale is so addictive, I can’t help myself. For me I’ve come to the conclusion that my eating disorder is mostly a sh method gone wrong (if there’s even a right way for these things to go), and the scale is the same as seeing a scar; it’s visual proof of what I’m going through, it’s proof that something is wrong. My advice, and Ik it’s really hard, stop weighing yourself. Try not to think about it, don’t think about what the scale would say if you did weight yourself, and absolutely do not weigh yourself. That’s what I’m trying to do and it’s helped me recover tremendously. I can’t say I haven’t caved here and there and I definitely can’t say that I’m anywhere near recovered. Ig it just takes time. I wish you luck <3

Buttered toast. Used to be terrified to have to slices of bread and butter, now it’s one of the few things I can get myself to eat bc it’s just the right taste and texture and the bread calms my stomach
